text:
maya: Heads-up — weird HF chat_template -> Redwood rendering bug. When a Jinja system block renders to an empty string (or just a newline) the next user role seems to inherit an extra leading sentinel/text fragment and instruction-following drops in our evals. Repro below.
kevin: Ugh. Can you paste the Jinja snippet and the Redwood output?

rachel: Seen similar once with special_tokens getting mapped differently, could be tokenization or the conversion script trimming but leaving a sentinel.

maya: Repro. HF template (simplified):

```jinja
{%- if system_instructions -%}
- role: system
  content: |
    {{ system_instructions }}
{%- endif -%}
- role: user
  content: |
    {{ user_prompt }}
```

When system_instructions is empty string or "\n" we expect the conversion to drop system role entirely. But the Redwood prompt generator emits something like:

```txt
<SYSTEM>


USER: {{ user_prompt }}
```

Notice the blank lines and an extra hidden sentinel token between SYSTEM and USER. After tokenization the first tokens of user content are shifted (model sees a stray system-esque token).

andre: Do you have the exact config.json mapping for special tokens? Maybe we map "</s>" -> "<|endoftext|>" or similar and conversion inserts placeholders.

maya: From the model config we found: "special_tokens_map": {"bos_token":"","eos_token":"","sep_token":"<|sep|>"} and chat_template conversion code uses a reduce/replace that does: replace('\n\n', '\n<SENTINEL>\n') if role_block present. So empty system => sentinel remains with no content.

kevin: That matches. The conversion script is trying to ensure role separators exist, but it doesn't check for empty role content. So you get a sentinel with no content which is tokenized into a non-whitespace token by our tokenizer (esp. quantized vocab mapping).

rachel: Impact on evals?

maya: Ran quick eval-suite on instruction-following benchmark (dev/instr-follow/roundtrip). Baseline (native HF runner) pass@1 = 0.84. After conversion to Redwood->same model (float32) pass@1 = 0.66. Re-ran with a patched converter that drops empty roles: pass@1 = 0.83. Also saw larger failures on 4-bit quant runs — suspected because quantized tokenizer embedding table merges sentinel into next token more aggressively.

andre: So two failure modes: (1) conversion leaves sentinel/placeholder for empty roles; (2) tokenizer / special token mapping interprets those placeholders as non-whitespace tokens, especially in quantized runs.

ci-bot: deploy-checklist: assign bug, add unit test for empty-role handling in chat_template converter, add regression test in eval-suite.

kevin: Proposed fix: converter should run through role blocks and if content.strip() == '' then omit the entire role block (including separators), not just the content. Also canonicalize special token placeholders to actual whitespace-only separators that tokenizer maps to nothing.

rachel: Agree. Also add a fuzz test: random combos of system/user/assistant empty vs whitespace content and assert Redwood prompt tokenization roundtrips to original roles.

maya: Will open PR with: 1) strict empty-role drop, 2) explicit sentinel token mapping to '\n<|role_sep|>\n' which our tokenizer maps to a single whitespace token, 3) add eval-suite run (float32 + 4-bit) to show regression fixed. ETA EOD.

andre: Thanks. If you can include one failing example from the wild (customer reported) in the PR that helps prioritize.

maya: Pasted one customer example in the issue — their prompt had an optional system note that was empty for mobile clients, triggered the regression.

kevin: Nice catch. :+1:

maya: Filing issue now. Link will be in the PR. Thanks all.
